ROW.COLUMN: (FR/CU) Account Registration or Control Change Followed by Disbursement

Many instances of fraud, such as identity theft, are perpetrated through illegal access to customer accounts by third parties who then use this access to make changes to account or customer information, registration information, or account control information. Although these types of changes are often done for legitimate purposes, they are of particular concern when followed within a short period by a disbursement of funds from the account. This scenario monitors for account changes followed by a disbursement that could indicate fraudulent activity, such as account takeover. The changes that trigger scrutiny include the following: - Change in key account information to gain access to the account or prevent the legitimate owner of the account from knowing that funds are being diverted. - Change in key account registration information to gain access to the account or prevent account officers from contacting the legitimate owner of the account (that is, mailing address or telephone number change). - Change in the list of entities authorized to move account assets.
